validation_boundary: Source-guided scouting only. ASTRA packets remain source-derived/unreviewed; this scout did not independently reconstruct their proofs. Historical priority and external mathematical validation are unknown.

opportunities.confidence: high as a strategic target; no new theorem obtained

exact_target.quantifiers: For every characteristic-zero field F, n,s,D >= 1, and every commutative arithmetic circuit over F of size at most s and formal degree at most D computing a nonzero P in F[x_1,...,x_n], prove an explicit uniform B(n,s,D) polynomial in n,s,D such that ord_{z=0} P(log(1+z),...,log(1+z/n)) < B(n,s,D); alternatively exhibit a uniform polynomial-size circuit family with superpolynomial contact.
exact_target.coefficient_contract: Circuit constants may be arbitrary elements of F; B is independent of their encodings. The logarithms are formal power series over F via the canonical characteristic-zero embedding of Q.
exact_target.cost_contract: Circuit size and degree are charged. The sufficient PIT reduction has polynomially many rational generator points with polynomial bit-length; black-box circuit-evaluation cost is separate.
exact_target.consequence_if_proved: Truncate each logarithm at L=B terms. P(phi_1,...,phi_n) remains nonzero and has degree at most D(L-1), so D(L-1)+1 distinct rational evaluations form a deterministic black-box hitting set. This is sufficient for general characteristic-zero commutative circuit PIT, not necessary for every PIT approach.

opportunities.historical_significance: A polynomial contact theorem would give a deterministic black-box PIT generator for general commutative circuits in characteristic zero.
opportunities.hidden_source_mechanism: OpenAI Math's noncommutative formula construction preserves exponentially many words using linearly independent iterated integrals, converts formulas to O(s)-state rational differential systems, applies a Wronskian/Moura multiplicity bound, and truncates into explicit matrices. Its positive-characteristic companion also uses finite local-coefficient rings and multiplication-matrix descent to control field extensions and bit costs. The shared-circuit step is missing: the source formulas/path programs have small state, whereas generic shared circuits need not.
opportunities.load_bearing_lemma: A circuit-operation-sensitive bound on the first nonzero Taylor coefficient of the nonlinear readout P(log(1+z/i)), without constructing an exponentially large derivative closure or faithful linear realization.

strongest_prior_art.source: Shubham Bhardwaj and Ramprasad Saptharishi, Hitting Sets for Polynomials with Small Partial Derivative Spaces, arXiv:2609.34436v1
strongest_prior_art.scope: Explicit poly(n,d,r) hitting sets over characteristic-zero fields when partial-derivative-space dimension is at most r; includes depth-3 powering. Does not establish a polynomial derivative-space bound or the contact theorem for arbitrary shared circuits.

strongest_prior_art.source: OpenAI Math, One Rational Matrix Hitting Point for Noncommutative Formulas, source version pinned above
strongest_prior_art.scope: Deterministic rational matrix hitting point for noncommutative formulas; its introduction explicitly says it asserts no bound for arbitrary shared circuits.

strongest_prior_art.source: OpenAI Math, Uniform Matrix Hitting Points in Every Positive Characteristic, source version pinned above
strongest_prior_art.scope: Uniform simultaneous hitting tuple for bounded-size noncommutative formulas over extension fields in positive characteristic; formula scope only.

opportunities.early_falsification: Use exact rational-series/Hankel computations to search for a small circuit family whose contact grows superpolynomially in its encoding size; treat finite instances as falsifier discovery only. Test proposed recurrences against products and powers whose derivative-space dimension is large while contact is only linear.
opportunities.significance_if_established: General deterministic black-box PIT for characteristic-zero commutative arithmetic circuits, with an explicit generator and bit-cost accounting.
limitations: N246's exponential derivative-space/linear-realization dimension is a representation barrier, not a lower bound on direct nonlinear contact or general PIT.
The prior small-derivative hitting set is not new work and does not settle the gate.
ASTRA's N250 source package is source-derived/unreviewed; no new proof reconstruction or formal validation occurred here.

exact_target.input: A length-m physical EPR gate word W with G_e=a_e I+c_e C+d_e D, C=2|psi+><psi+|, D=(X tensor X)SWAP, rational a_e>0 and c_e,d_e>=0, physical equality sewing on every wire, and B-bit rational parameters/topology included in the input.
exact_target.quantity: The exact equality-sewn tensor contraction Z(W).
exact_target.desired_reduction: Construct in time poly(m,B) either (i) an exact known-factor reduction of Z(W) to a specified coefficient [x^alpha](g_mu g_nu), where g_mu and g_nu are nonnegative multiaffine log-concave polynomials over a polynomial-size ground set, or (ii) a parsimonious reduction to counting common integer bases of two integral polymatroids with polynomial-time exact rank-value oracles and binary-encoded ranks.
exact_target.algorithmic_completion: For route (i), acquire evaluation oracles, nonzero support initializers, coefficient-range bounds, and polynomial bit costs; Chen-Liu Theorem 1.6 then gives an FPRAS for the coefficient. For route (ii), use the OpenAI common-integer-polymatroid FPRAS, including its rank-oracle and binary-input cost contract. The full target is relative error epsilon with success probability at least 3/4 in bit time poly(m,B,epsilon^-1).

opportunities.hidden_source_mechanism: The OpenAI polymatroid source proves addition/removal quadratic-signature conditions for rank factors, closure under balanced summation, and factorial lifts that count unlabelled balanced profiles despite binary-scale capacities. At one physical wire, x=y is equivalent to x+(1-y)=1 after complementing the second selector; this identifies a balanced-pair lift worth testing. It does not imply the resulting gate weights satisfy signatures or log-concavity.

strongest_prior_art.source: Xiaoyu Chen and Kuikui Liu, An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids, arXiv:2610.06724v1
strongest_prior_art.scope: Theorem 1.6 handles specified coefficients of products of two nonnegative log-concave generating polynomials from evaluation oracles, given nonzero support initializers and coefficient-range upper bounds; its stated bound counts arithmetic operations and oracle calls. Appendix C.7 gives FPRAS results for the EPR Hamiltonian on arbitrary loopless graphs and Quantum Max-Cut on bipartite graphs. This does not by itself prove an FPRAS or reduction for arbitrary EPR gate-word contractions.

strongest_prior_art.source: OpenAI Math, An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities, source version pinned above
strongest_prior_art.scope: Counts unweighted common integer bases from exact value oracles for two integral normalized submodular ranks with equal binary-encoded total rank; no direct EPR reduction is supplied.

opportunities.early_falsification: Attempt the complemented one-hot selector lift on the smallest identity gate, one nonidentity gate, and the N193 bowtie interleaving. Check exact equality of the contraction, rank/value oracle validity, positivity on the full required domain, and every addition/removal signature. A failure of the unchanged [I|A|I+A] encoding is already known; only an alternative lift counts as progress.
opportunities.significance_if_established: An FPRAS for a circuit-contraction family beyond the EPR Hamiltonian/QMaxCut applications, with the exact support, precision, and bit-time interfaces acquired.
limitations: N190 supplies an exact positive determinant-square expectation, not polynomial relative variance or an FPRAS.
N191 refutes a universal all-gauges variance barrier, while exhibiting exponential relative second moment for specified legal nonidentity families and gauges.
N193's bowtie blocks naive scalar gluing; its one-gate identity transition blocks only the unchanged [I|A|I+A] basis encoding, not all lifts.
N192's consecutive cactus compiler is already exactly solvable by transfer dynamic programming and does not cover arbitrary interleavings or repeated gates.

The Chen-Liu FPRAS has oracle, log-concavity, initializer, coefficient-range, and finite-bit obligations; the OpenAI polymatroid theorem counts unweighted common integer bases. Neither is a turnkey compiler for Z(W).

mipco.primary_claim: Junqiao Lin's official arXiv v1 claims MIPco=coRE using compression and tracially embeddable strategies.
mipco.scope: ASTRA N183's exact CHSH counterexample targets the specified symmetric processed-Bob-private-prefix completion/equality fallback only. N242 shows an ideal recognized event probability 1/3 cannot be realized exactly by a finite uniform binary seed; the adjusted four-role/prefix wire and all later compression stages remain unaudited. Neither result refutes MIPco=coRE or arbitrary asymmetric completions.
mipco.audit_action: Exact source/parser/sampler and downstream register audit; do not advertise a theorem refutation from the scoped CHSH fixture or non-dyadic ideal law.

conditional_sampler.scope: N95's positive-word approximation requires nonnegative matrices, acquired support/minimum-entry information, and explicit precision/cost. N109 is conditional on Chen-Liu's theorem and a finite-bit interface. No end-to-end compiler is acquired.
